'''山形県護国神社'''（みやぎけんごこくじんじゃ）は[[山形県]][[山形市]]にある[[神社]]（[[護国神社]]）である。[[明治維新]]から[[第二次世界大戦]]までの殉国者3万9千余柱の[[英霊]]を祀る。
== 歴史 == [[明治]]2年（[[1869年]]）1月、[[戊辰戦争]]で戦死した[[薩摩藩]]士10柱を祀るために山形市八日町に社殿を造営したのに始まる。明治8年に山形[[招魂社]]となり、以降、山形県関係の殉国者を合祀した。明治21年、千歳公園内の現在地に遷座した。[[昭和]]14年（[[1939年]]）の制度改革により内務大臣指定護国神社となり、山形県護国神社と称した。GHQ占領下においては「千歳宮」と称していた。

Gokoku-jinja longshot.jpg|thumb|250px|大鳥居（奥に拝殿）]] '''山形県護国神社'''（やまがたけんごこくじんじゃ）は、[[山形県]][[山形市]]にある[[神社]]（[[護国神社]]）である。[[明治維新]]から[[第二次世界大戦]]までの殉国者4万余柱の[[英霊]]を祀る。 == 歴史 == [[明治]]2年（[[1869年]]）1月、[[戊辰戦争]]で戦死した[[薩摩藩]]士10柱を祀るために山形市八日町に社殿を造営したのに始まる。明治8年に山形[[招魂社]]となり、以降山形県関係の殉国者を合祀した。[[明治]]22年（[[1889年]]）山形市宮町に遷座し、[[明治]]44年（[[1911年]]）の山形市北大火の災厄で社殿焼失の憂き目に遭ったが、[[大正]]3年（[[1914年]]）に再建された。[[昭和]]9年（[[1934年]]）千歳公園内の現在地に遷座した。[[昭和]]14年（[[1939年]]）の制度改革により内務大臣指定護国神社となり、山形県護国神社と称した。GHQ占領下の[[昭和]]22年（[[1947年]]）から[[昭和]]27年（[[1952年]]）においては所在地の千歳公園に因んで「千歳宮」と称していた。現在の拝殿は[[平成]]6年（[[1994年]]）に改築されたものである。 == 初詣 == [[初詣]]の参拝客は例年山形県内で最も多く、約13万人となっている[http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/history.shtml 御由緒]. 公式サイトより[http://yamagata-np.jp/news/200901/05/kj_2009010500051.php 県内の初詣で91万6000人　前年比3万3000人増]. ''山形新聞''. (2009年01月05日). 2011年9月7日閲覧。[http://yamagata-np.jp/news/201101/04/kj_2011010400048.php 閉塞感打開へ「最後は神頼み？」　初詣に100万人超、過去10年で最多] ''山形新聞''. (2011年01月04日). 2011年9月7日閲覧。。第2位は同じく山形市内の[[鳥海月山両所宮]]（約11万人）で、10万人を超えるのは県内ではこの二社のみである。 == 脚注 ==

{{出典の明記|date=2017年8月28日 (月) 09:06 (UTC)}} {{神社| 名称=山形県護国神社| 所在地=[[山形県]][[山形市]]薬師町2-8-75| 位置={{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|38|15|45.23|N|140|20|49.86|E|scale:25000|region:JP-06_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=山形県護国神社}}| 祭神=護国の英霊　四万八百四十五柱| 社格=旧内務大臣指定護国神社・別表神社| 創建=[[明治]]2年（[[1869年]]）| 例祭=[[5月11日]]・[[11月2日]]| 画像=[[File:Yamagata Pref. Gokoku-jinja honden.jpg|220px]]
拝殿 |地図={{Location map|Japan Yamagata|lat_deg=38|lat_min=15|lat_sec=45.23|lon_deg=140|lon_min=20|lon_sec=49.86|label=山形県護国神社|position=center|width=200|float=center}}}} [[File:Yamagata Pref. Gokoku-jinja longshot.jpg|thumb|250px|大鳥居（奥に拝殿）]] '''山形県護国神社'''（やまがたけんごこくじんじゃ）は、[[山形県]][[山形市]]にある[[神社]]（[[護国神社]]）である。[[明治維新]]から[[第二次世界大戦]]までの戦没者4万余柱を祀る。 == 歴史 == [[明治]]2年（[[1869年]]）1月、[[戊辰戦争]]で戦死した[[薩摩藩]]士10柱を祀るために山形市八日町に社殿を造営したのに始まる。明治8年に山形[[招魂社]]となり、以降山形県関係の戦没者を合祀した。[[明治]]22年（[[1889年]]）山形市宮町に遷座し、[[明治]]44年（[[1911年]]）の山形市北大火の災厄で社殿焼失の憂き目に遭ったが、[[大正]]3年（[[1914年]]）に再建された。[[昭和]]9年（[[1934年]]）千歳公園内の現在地に遷座した。[[昭和]]14年（[[1939年]]）の制度改革により内務大臣指定護国神社となり、山形県護国神社と称した。GHQ占領下の[[昭和]]22年（[[1947年]]）から[[昭和]]27年（[[1952年]]）においては所在地の千歳公園に因んで「千歳宮」と称していた。現在の拝殿は[[平成]]6年（[[1994年]]）に改築されたものである。 == 初詣 == [[初詣]]の参拝客は例年山形県内で最も多く、約13万人となっている[http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/history.shtml 御由緒]. 公式サイトより[http://yamagata-np.jp/news/200901/05/kj_2009010500051.php 県内の初詣で91万6000人　前年比3万3000人増]. ''山形新聞''. (2009年01月05日). 2011年9月7日閲覧。[http://yamagata-np.jp/news/201101/04/kj_2011010400048.php 閉塞感打開へ「最後は神頼み？」　初詣に100万人超、過去10年で最多] ''山形新聞''. (2011年1月4日). 2011年9月7日閲覧。。第2位は同じく山形市内の[[鳥海月山両所宮]]（約11万人）で、10万人を超えるのは県内ではこの二社のみである。 == 脚注 ==
==外部リンク== *[http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/ 山形県護国神社]（公式サイト）

{{draft}} {{Infobox religious building | native_name = 護国神社 | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | map_type = Japan | coordinates = | map_size = | map_alt = | map_relief = | map_caption = | location = | festival = | type = ''[[Gokoku shrine]]''
(Formerly ''[[Shokonsha]]'') | leadership = | website = | architecture_style = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = }} {{Ill|{{PAGENAME}}|ja|護国神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this [[WP:BLUE]] considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |issn=0021-969X}} == See Also == * [[Controversies surrounding Yasukuni Shrine]] * [[Hero shrine]] * [[Martial temple]] and [[Wen Wu temple]] * [[National Revolutionary Martyrs' Shrine]] * [[Eternal Spring Shrine]] * [[Chinese Cultural Renaissance]] * [[Ancestral shrine]] * [[Gallant Garden]] * [[Gokoku Shrines]] * [[Tomb of the Unknown Soldier]] * [[Arlington National Cemetery]] * [[Valhalla]] (home to the souls of fallen warriors in Scandinavian mythology) * [[Walhalla (memorial)|Walhalla Shrine]] (a hall of fame in Germany honoring "commendable and honorable Germans") * [[Eternal Spring Shrine]] * [[The common end of myriad good deeds]] * [[Greek hero cult]] == Notes == {{Notelist}} == References == {{reflist}} {{Draft categories| [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Gokoku shrines]] }}

(Formerly ''[[Shokonsha]]'') | leadership = | website = | architecture_style = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = }}[[ja:山形県護国神社]] {{Ill|{{PAGENAME}}|ja|山形県護国神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it. It was founded in 1868, and is located in [[Yamagata Prefecture]].{{Cite web |last=Yassan |date=2021-11-29 |title=Tiger in Yamagata prefecture Gokoku shrine, Yamagata City 25km |url=https://gpsart.info/en/tohoku-2/tiger-in-yamagata-prefecture-gokoku-shrine-yamagata-city-25km/ |access-date=2023-11-27 |website=GPS Art .info |language=en-GB}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead. Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |doi=10.1093/jcs/32.3.527 |jstor=23917081 |issn=0021-969X}} == New years festival == The shrine has the largest [[Hatsumōde]] festival of [[Yamagata Prefecture]] with 130,000 people attending. (Formerly ''[[Shokonsha]]'') | leadership = | website = | architecture_style = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = }}[[ja:山形県護国神社]] {{Ill|{{PAGENAME}}|ja|山形県護国神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it. It was founded in 1868, and is located in [[Yamagata Prefecture]].{{Cite web |last=Yassan |date=2021-11-29 |title=Tiger in Yamagata prefecture Gokoku shrine, Yamagata City 25km |url=https://gpsart.info/en/tohoku-2/tiger-in-yamagata-prefecture-gokoku-shrine-yamagata-city-25km/ |access-date=2023-11-27 |website=GPS Art .info |language=en-GB}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead. Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |doi=10.1093/jcs/32.3.527 |jstor=23917081 |issn=0021-969X}} == New years festival == The shrine has the largest [[Hatsumōde]] festival of [[Yamagata Prefecture]] with 130,000 people attending. So now addiing [[:Category:draft articles]] is the new one As with the previous the idea behind this is that this designates any given draft to happen on a specific weekend day. A draft cannot be bumped twice, so they cannot end up floating to the top with being rebumped. == Draft notes == Due to [[Wikipedia:Categories for discussion/Log/2023 July 21#Category:Secondary School Kanji]] almost all Joyo kanji here have the exact same expiration date. {{AFC submission|d|v|u=Immanuelle|ns=118|decliner=DoubleGrazing|declinets=20230828082727|reason2=nn|ts=20230425024001}} {{Short description|Shinto shrine}} {{Draft topics|east-asia}} {{AfC topic|geo}} {{draft}} {{afc comment|1=like {{ill|Chōkai gassan ryōsho-gu|simple|Chōkai gassan ryōsho-gu|ja|鳥海月山両所宮|draft}} I like this shrine but I'm not sure whether it is a feasible one or independently notable enough[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 00:17, 17 November 2023 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building | native_name = 護国神社 | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Yamagata Pref. Gokoku-jinja honden.jpg | map_type = Japan | coordinates = | map_size = | map_alt = | map_relief = | map_caption = | location = | festival = | type = ''[[Gokoku shrine]]''
(Formerly ''[[Shokonsha]]'') | leadership = | website = | architecture_style = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = }}[[ja:山形県護国神社]] {{Ill|{{PAGENAME}}|ja|山形県護国神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it. It was founded in 1868, and is located in [[Yamagata Prefecture]].{{Cite web |last=Yassan |date=2021-11-29 |title=Tiger in Yamagata prefecture Gokoku shrine, Yamagata City 25km |url=https://gpsart.info/en/tohoku-2/tiger-in-yamagata-prefecture-gokoku-shrine-yamagata-city-25km/ |access-date=2023-11-27 |website=GPS Art .info |language=en-GB}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead. Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |doi=10.1093/jcs/32.3.527 |jstor=23917081 |issn=0021-969X}} == New years festival == The shrine has the largest [[Hatsumōde]] festival of [[Yamagata Prefecture]] with 130,000 people attending. Second most is {{ill|Chōkai gassan ryōsho-gu|simple|Chōkai gassan ryōsho-gu|ja|鳥海月山両所宮|draft}} == See Also == * [[Controversies surrounding Yasukuni Shrine]] * [[Hero shrine]] * [[Martial temple]] and [[Wen Wu temple]] * [[National Revolutionary Martyrs' Shrine]] * [[Eternal Spring Shrine]] * [[Chinese Cultural Renaissance]] * [[Ancestral shrine]] * [[Gallant Garden]] * [[Gokoku Shrines]] * [[Tomb of the Unknown Soldier]] * [[Arlington National Cemetery]] * [[Valhalla]] (home to the souls of fallen warriors in Scandinavian mythology) * [[Walhalla (memorial)|Walhalla Shrine]] (a hall of fame in Germany honoring "commendable and honorable Germans") * [[Eternal Spring Shrine]] * [[The common end of myriad good deeds]] * [[Greek hero cult]] == References == {{reflist}} {{Draft categories| [[:Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[:Category:Gokoku shrines]] [[:Category:1869 establishments]] [[:Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[:Category:Yamagata Prefecture]] [[category:drafts]] [[Category:Draft articles]] [[Category:Bumping is back but only bump on Monday and Tuesday, this ensures deletion messages only come in on weekends where I have time to reasonably look over them Previous bumping worked by adding [[:Category:wikipedia drafts]] but that was overused. So now addiing [[:Category:draft articles]] is the new one As with the previous the idea behind this is that this designates any given draft to happen on a specific weekend day. A draft cannot be bumped twice, so they cannot end up floating to the top with being rebumped. == Draft notes == Due to [[Wikipedia:Categories for discussion/Log/2023 July 21#Category:Secondary School Kanji]] almost all Joyo kanji here have the exact same expiration date. On January 8 they will all simultaneously go onto my talk page, and on February 8 they will all be simultaneously deleted. I’ll have a later time around February 17 to March 17 where initially a glut of [[kyoiku kanji]] will come, followed by a lot of articles I bumped during the ani over the kanji, either over attempting to make them presentable and submittable or over bumping ones that would pop up in the weeks after October 22 so I’d have more time to get articles complete before getting bombarded with g13 deletions I’d no longer be able to stop. On Monday November 27, 2023 I started bumping again These bumped articles will have their g17 warnings on Saturday April 27, 2024 I will bump again on Tuesday November 28, 2023, These bumped articles will have their g17 warnings on Sunday April 28, 2024 I updated the draft table to the derived from tools one rather than the derived from talk page one, since enough were already bumped it was irrelevant that they came from the talk page I needed to clear a large portion of drafts out so the page size limit was not exceeded. When I get my draft count down to 2,946 drafts I believe it will be good to have all drafts in the table. {{AFC submission|d|v|u=Immanuelle|ns=118|decliner=DoubleGrazing|declinets=20230828082727|reason2=nn|ts=20230425024001}} {{Short description|Shinto shrine}} {{Draft topics|east-asia}} {{AfC topic|geo}} {{draft}} {{afc comment|1=like {{ill|Chōkai gassan ryōsho-gu|simple|Chōkai gassan ryōsho-gu|ja|鳥海月山両所宮|draft}} I like this shrine but I'm not sure whether it is a feasible one or independently notable enough[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 00:17, 17 November 2023 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building | native_name = 護国神社 | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Yamagata Pref. Gokoku-jinja honden.jpg | map_type = Japan | coordinates = | map_size = | map_alt = | map_relief = | map_caption = | location = | festival = | type = ''[[Gokoku shrine]]''
(Formerly ''[[Shokonsha]]'') | leadership = | website = | architecture_style = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = }}[[ja:山形県護国神社]] {{Ill|{{PAGENAME}}|ja|山形県護国神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it. It was founded in 1868, and is located in [[Yamagata Prefecture]].{{Cite web |last=Yassan |date=2021-11-29 |title=Tiger in Yamagata prefecture Gokoku shrine, Yamagata City 25km |url=https://gpsart.info/en/tohoku-2/tiger-in-yamagata-prefecture-gokoku-shrine-yamagata-city-25km/ |access-date=2023-11-27 |website=GPS Art .info |language=en-GB}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead. Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |doi=10.1093/jcs/32.3.527 |jstor=23917081 |issn=0021-969X}} == New years festival == The shrine has the largest [[Hatsumōde]] festival of [[Yamagata Prefecture]] with 130,000 people attending. Second most is {{ill|Chōkai gassan ryōsho-gu|simple|Chōkai gassan ryōsho-gu|ja|鳥海月山両所宮|draft}} == See Also == * [[Controversies surrounding Yasukuni Shrine]] * [[Hero shrine]] * [[Martial temple]] and [[Wen Wu temple]] * [[National Revolutionary Martyrs' Shrine]] * [[Eternal Spring Shrine]] * [[Chinese Cultural Renaissance]] * [[Ancestral shrine]] * [[Gallant Garden]] * [[Gokoku Shrines]] * [[Tomb of the Unknown Soldier]] * [[Arlington National Cemetery]] * [[Valhalla]] (home to the souls of fallen warriors in Scandinavian mythology) * [[Walhalla (memorial)|Walhalla Shrine]] (a hall of fame in Germany honoring "commendable and honorable Germans") * [[Eternal Spring Shrine]] * [[The common end of myriad good deeds]] * [[Greek hero cult]] == References == {{reflist}} {{Draft categories| [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Gokoku shrines]] [[Category:1869 establishments]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[Category:Yamagata Prefecture]] [[category:drafts]] [[Category:Draft articles]] }}

Gokoku-jinja longshot.jpg|thumb|250px|Ōtorii (and haiden in the background)]] '''Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja''' (山形県護国神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Gokoku Shrine|ja|護国神社}}) located in {{ill|Yamagata (city)|ja|山形市}}, {{ill|Yamagata Prefecture|ja|山形県}}. It enshrines over 48,000 spirits of those from Yamagata Prefecture who died in wars from the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} through the {{ill|Second Sino-Japanese War|ja|日中戦争}} and {{ill|World War II|ja|第二次世界大戦}}. == History == The shrine traces its origins to Meiji 2 (1869), when a hall was constructed in Yōka-chō, Yamagata City, to enshrine the spirits of ten {{ill|Satsuma Domain|ja|薩摩藩}} soldiers who died in the {{ill|Boshin War|ja|戊辰戦争}}. In Meiji 8, it was designated as Yamagata {{ill|Shōkonsha|ja|招魂社}}, and subsequently enshrined war dead from Yamagata Prefecture. In Meiji 22 (1889), it was relocated to Miyamachi, Yamagata City, but was destroyed by fire in a large blaze in 1911 (Meiji 44), and rebuilt in 1914 (Taishō 3). In Shōwa 9 (1934), it moved to its current location inside Chitose Park. In Shōwa 14 (1939), with institutional reforms, it was designated as an Interior Minister-approved Gokoku Jinja and named Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja. Under the Allied Occupation, from Shōwa 22 (1947) to Shōwa 27 (1952), it was called “Chitose-gū,” referencing Chitose Park. The current haiden was rebuilt in Heisei 6 (1994). == Hatsumōde (First Shrine Visit of the New Year) == Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja attracts the largest number of hatsumōde (New Year’s first visits) worshippers in Yamagata Prefecture, with about 130,000 visitors annually.[http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/history.shtml Official site: History (in Japanese)][http://yamagata-np.jp/news/200901/05/kj_2009010500051.php “91,6000 People Visit Shrines in the Prefecture for New Year: Up by 33,000 from Last Year”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 5, 2009), accessed September 7, 2011.[http://yamagata-np.jp/news/201101/04/kj_2011010400048.php “Over 1 Million Visit Shrines for Hatsumōde in Prefecture, Highest in a Decade”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 4, 2011), accessed September 7, 2011. The second most visited shrine is {{ill|Chōkai Gassan Ryōsho-gū|ja|鳥海月山両所宮}} in Yamagata City (~110,000 visitors). Only these two shrines surpass 100,000 visitors in the prefecture. == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/ Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja Official Site] {{Shinto Navbox}} {{Shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[Category:Gokoku Shrines]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrines]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Yamagata (city)]] [[Category:History of Yamagata (city)]] == New years festival == The shrine has the largest [[Hatsumōde]] festival of [[Yamagata Prefecture]] with 130,000 people attending. It was founded in 1868, and is located in [[Yamagata Prefecture]].{{Cite web |last=Yassan |date=2021-11-29 |title=Tiger in Yamagata prefecture Gokoku shrine, Yamagata City 25km |url=https://gpsart.info/en/tohoku-2/tiger-in-yamagata-prefecture-gokoku-shrine-yamagata-city-25km/ |access-date=2023-11-27 |website=GPS Art .info |language=en-GB}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead. Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. Gokoku-jinja longshot.jpg|thumb|250px|Ōtorii (and haiden in the background)]] '''Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja''' (山形県護国神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Gokoku Shrine|ja|護国神社}}) located in {{ill|Yamagata (city)|ja|山形市}}, {{ill|Yamagata Prefecture|ja|山形県}}. It enshrines over 48,000 spirits of those from Yamagata Prefecture who died in wars from the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} through the {{ill|Second Sino-Japanese War|ja|日中戦争}} and {{ill|World War II|ja|第二次世界大戦}}. == History == The shrine traces its origins to Meiji 2 (1869), when a hall was constructed in Yōka-chō, Yamagata City, to enshrine the spirits of ten {{ill|Satsuma Domain|ja|薩摩藩}} soldiers who died in the {{ill|Boshin War|ja|戊辰戦争}}. In Meiji 8, it was designated as Yamagata {{ill|Shōkonsha|ja|招魂社}}, and subsequently enshrined war dead from Yamagata Prefecture. In Meiji 22 (1889), it was relocated to Miyamachi, Yamagata City, but was destroyed by fire in a large blaze in 1911 (Meiji 44), and rebuilt in 1914 (Taishō 3). In Shōwa 9 (1934), it moved to its current location inside Chitose Park. In Shōwa 14 (1939), with institutional reforms, it was designated as an Interior Minister-approved Gokoku Jinja and named Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja. Under the Allied Occupation, from Shōwa 22 (1947) to Shōwa 27 (1952), it was called “Chitose-gū,” referencing Chitose Park. The current haiden was rebuilt in Heisei 6 (1994). == Hatsumōde (First Shrine Visit of the New Year) == Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja attracts the largest number of hatsumōde (New Year’s first visits) worshippers in Yamagata Prefecture, with about 130,000 visitors annually.[http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/history.shtml Official site: History (in Japanese)][http://yamagata-np.jp/news/200901/05/kj_2009010500051.php “91,6000 People Visit Shrines in the Prefecture for New Year: Up by 33,000 from Last Year”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 5, 2009), accessed September 7, 2011.[http://yamagata-np.jp/news/201101/04/kj_2011010400048.php “Over 1 Million Visit Shrines for Hatsumōde in Prefecture, Highest in a Decade”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 4, 2011), accessed September 7, 2011. The second most visited shrine is {{ill|Chōkai Gassan Ryōsho-gū|ja|鳥海月山両所宮}} in Yamagata City (~110,000 visitors). Only these two shrines surpass 100,000 visitors in the prefecture. == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/ Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja Official Site] {{Shinto Navbox}} {{Shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrines]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Yamagata (city)]] [[Category:History of Yamagata (city)]] == New years festival == The shrine has the largest [[Hatsumōde]] festival of [[Yamagata Prefecture]] with 130,000 people attending. Second most is {{ill|Chōkai gassan ryōsho-gu|simple|Chōkai gassan ryōsho-gu|ja|鳥海月山両所宮|draft}} == See Also == * [[Controversies surrounding Yasukuni Shrine]] * [[Hero shrine]] * [[Martial temple]] and [[Wen Wu temple]] * [[National Revolutionary Martyrs' Shrine]] * [[Eternal Spring Shrine]] * [[Chinese Cultural Renaissance]] * [[Ancestral shrine]] * [[Gallant Garden]] * [[Gokoku Shrines]] * [[Tomb of the Unknown Soldier]] * [[Arlington National Cemetery]] * [[Valhalla]] (home to the souls of fallen warriors in Scandinavian mythology) * [[Walhalla (memorial)|Walhalla Shrine]] (a hall of fame in Germany honoring "commendable and honorable Germans") * [[Eternal Spring Shrine]] * [[The common end of myriad good deeds]] * [[Greek hero cult]] == References == {{reflist}} {{Draft categories| [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Gokoku shrines]] [[Category:Gokoku shrines]]{{Gokoku Shrines}}[[Category:Gokoku shrines]] [[Category:1869 establishments]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[Category:Yamagata Prefecture]] [[category:drafts]] [[Category:Original pages]] }}

Gokoku-jinja longshot.jpg|thumb|250px|Ōtorii (and haiden in the background)]] '''Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja''' (山形県護国神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Gokoku Shrine|ja|護国神社}}) located in {{ill|Yamagata (city)|ja|山形市}}, {{ill|Yamagata Prefecture|ja|山形県}}. It enshrines over 48,000 spirits of those from Yamagata Prefecture who died in wars from the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} through the {{ill|Second Sino-Japanese War|ja|日中戦争}} and {{ill|World War II|ja|第二次世界大戦}}. == History == The shrine traces its origins to Meiji 2 (1869), when a hall was constructed in Yōka-chō, Yamagata City, to enshrine the spirits of ten {{ill|Satsuma Domain|ja|薩摩藩}} soldiers who died in the {{ill|Boshin War|ja|戊辰戦争}}. In Meiji 8, it was designated as Yamagata {{ill|Shōkonsha|ja|招魂社}}, and subsequently enshrined war dead from Yamagata Prefecture. In Meiji 22 (1889), it was relocated to Miyamachi, Yamagata City, but was destroyed by fire in a large blaze in 1911 (Meiji 44), and rebuilt in 1914 (Taishō 3). In Shōwa 9 (1934), it moved to its current location inside Chitose Park. In Shōwa 14 (1939), with institutional reforms, it was designated as an Interior Minister-approved Gokoku Jinja and named Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja. Under the Allied Occupation, from Shōwa 22 (1947) to Shōwa 27 (1952), it was called “Chitose-gū,” referencing Chitose Park. The current haiden was rebuilt in Heisei 6 (1994). == Hatsumōde (First Shrine Visit of the New Year) == Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja attracts the largest number of hatsumōde (New Year’s first visits) worshippers in Yamagata Prefecture, with about 130,000 visitors annually.[http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/history.shtml Official site: History (in Japanese)][http://yamagata-np.jp/news/200901/05/kj_2009010500051.php “91,6000 People Visit Shrines in the Prefecture for New Year: Up by 33,000 from Last Year”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 5, 2009), accessed September 7, 2011.[http://yamagata-np.jp/news/201101/04/kj_2011010400048.php “Over 1 Million Visit Shrines for Hatsumōde in Prefecture, Highest in a Decade”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 4, 2011), accessed September 7, 2011. The second most visited shrine is {{ill|Chōkai Gassan Ryōsho-gū|ja|鳥海月山両所宮}} in Yamagata City (~110,000 visitors). It enshrines over 48,000 spirits of those from Yamagata Prefecture who died in wars from the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} through the {{ill|Second Sino-Japanese War|ja|日中戦争}} and {{ill|World War II|ja|第二次世界大戦}}. == History == The shrine traces its origins to Meiji 2 (1869), when a hall was constructed in Yōka-chō, Yamagata City, to enshrine the spirits of ten {{ill|Satsuma Domain|ja|薩摩藩}} soldiers who died in the {{ill|Boshin War|ja|戊辰戦争}}. In Meiji 8, it was designated as Yamagata {{ill|Shōkonsha|ja|招魂社}}, and subsequently enshrined war dead from Yamagata Prefecture. In Meiji 22 (1889), it was relocated to Miyamachi, Yamagata City, but was destroyed by fire in a large blaze in 1911 (Meiji 44), and rebuilt in 1914 (Taishō 3). In Shōwa 9 (1934), it moved to its current location inside Chitose Park. In Shōwa 14 (1939), with institutional reforms, it was designated as an Interior Minister-approved Gokoku Jinja and named Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja. Under the Allied Occupation, from Shōwa 22 (1947) to Shōwa 27 (1952), it was called “Chitose-gū,” referencing Chitose Park. The current haiden was rebuilt in Heisei 6 (1994). == Hatsumōde (First Shrine Visit of the New Year) == Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja attracts the largest number of hatsumōde (New Year’s first visits) worshippers in Yamagata Prefecture, with about 130,000 visitors annually.[http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/history.shtml Official site: History (in Japanese)][http://yamagata-np.jp/news/200901/05/kj_2009010500051.php “91,6000 People Visit Shrines in the Prefecture for New Year: Up by 33,000 from Last Year”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 5, 2009), accessed September 7, 2011.[http://yamagata-np.jp/news/201101/04/kj_2011010400048.php “Over 1 Million Visit Shrines for Hatsumōde in Prefecture, Highest in a Decade”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 4, 2011), accessed September 7, 2011. The second most visited shrine is {{ill|Chōkai Gassan Ryōsho-gū|ja|鳥海月山両所宮}} in Yamagata City (~110,000 visitors). Only these two shrines surpass 100,000 visitors in the prefecture. == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/ Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja Official Site] {{Shinto Navbox}} {{Shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrines]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Yamagata (city)]] [[Category:History of Yamagata (city)]] == New years festival == The shrine has the largest [[Hatsumōde]] festival of [[Yamagata Prefecture]] with 130,000 people attending. Gokoku-jinja longshot.jpg|thumb|250px|Ōtorii (and haiden in the background)]] '''Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja''' (山形県護国神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Gokoku Shrine|ja|護国神社}}) located in {{ill|Yamagata (city)|ja|山形市}}, {{ill|Yamagata Prefecture|ja|山形県}}. It enshrines over 48,000 spirits of those from Yamagata Prefecture who died in wars from the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} through the {{ill|Second Sino-Japanese War|ja|日中戦争}} and {{ill|World War II|ja|第二次世界大戦}}. == History == The shrine traces its origins to Meiji 2 (1869), when a hall was constructed in Yōka-chō, Yamagata City, to enshrine the spirits of ten {{ill|Satsuma Domain|ja|薩摩藩}} soldiers who died in the {{ill|Boshin War|ja|戊辰戦争}}. In Meiji 8, it was designated as Yamagata {{ill|Shōkonsha|ja|招魂社}}, and subsequently enshrined war dead from Yamagata Prefecture. In Meiji 22 (1889), it was relocated to Miyamachi, Yamagata City, but was destroyed by fire in a large blaze in 1911 (Meiji 44), and rebuilt in 1914 (Taishō 3). In Shōwa 9 (1934), it moved to its current location inside Chitose Park. In Shōwa 14 (1939), with institutional reforms, it was designated as an Interior Minister-approved Gokoku Jinja and named Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja. Under the Allied Occupation, from Shōwa 22 (1947) to Shōwa 27 (1952), it was called “Chitose-gū,” referencing Chitose Park. The current haiden was rebuilt in Heisei 6 (1994). == Hatsumōde (First Shrine Visit of the New Year) == Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja attracts the largest number of hatsumōde (New Year’s first visits) worshippers in Yamagata Prefecture, with about 130,000 visitors annually.[http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/history.shtml Official site: History (in Japanese)][http://yamagata-np.jp/news/200901/05/kj_2009010500051.php “91,6000 People Visit Shrines in the Prefecture for New Year: Up by 33,000 from Last Year”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 5, 2009), accessed September 7, 2011.[http://yamagata-np.jp/news/201101/04/kj_2011010400048.php “Over 1 Million Visit Shrines for Hatsumōde in Prefecture, Highest in a Decade”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 4, 2011), accessed September 7, 2011. The second most visited shrine is {{ill|Chōkai Gassan Ryōsho-gū|ja|鳥海月山両所宮}} in Yamagata City (~110,000 visitors). Only these two shrines surpass 100,000 visitors in the prefecture. == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/ Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja Official Site] {{Shinto Navbox}} {{Shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrines]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Yamagata (city)]] [[Category:History of Yamagata (city)]] == New years festival == The shrine has the largest [[Hatsumōde]] festival of [[Yamagata Prefecture]] with 130,000 people attending. Second most is {{ill|Chōkai gassan ryōsho-gu|simple|Chōkai gassan ryōsho-gu|ja|鳥海月山両所宮|draft}} == See Also == * [[Controversies surrounding Yasukuni Shrine]] * [[Martyrs' shrines (China)|Martyr's Shrines]] * [[:en:Martial temple|Martial temple]] and [[:en:Wen Wu temple|Wen Wu temple]] * [[National Revolutionary Martyrs' Shrine]] * [[Eternal Spring Shrine]] * [[:en:Chinese Cultural Renaissance|Chinese Cultural Renaissance]] * [[Ancestral shrine]] * [[:en:Gallant Garden|Gallant Garden]] * [[Gokoku Shrines]] * [[:en:Tomb of the Unknown Soldier|Tomb of the Unknown Soldier]] * [[:en:Arlington National Cemetery|Arlington National Cemetery]] * [[:en:Valhalla|Valhalla]] (home to the souls of fallen warriors in Scandinavian mythology) * [[:en:Walhalla (memorial)|Walhalla Shrine]] (a hall of fame in Germany honoring "commendable and honorable Germans") * [[Eternal Spring Shrine]] * [[The common end of myriad good deeds]] * [[:en:Greek hero cult|Greek hero cult]] == References == {{reflist}} {{Draft categories| [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Gokoku shrines]] [[Category:Gokoku shrines]]{{Gokoku Shrines}}[[Category:Gokoku shrines]] [[Category:1869 establishments]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[Category:Yamagata Prefecture]] [[category:drafts]] [[Category:Original pages]] [[Category:original pages]][[Category:original pages]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from wikipedia5]][[en:Yamagata Gokoku Shrine]][[Category:Pages and Categories from wikipedia5]] [[Category:Pages from wikipedia]] }}

Gokoku-jinja longshot.jpg|thumb|250px|Ōtorii (and haiden in the background)]] '''Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja''' (山形県護国神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Gokoku Shrine|ja|護国神社}}) located in {{ill|Yamagata (city)|ja|山形市}}, {{ill|Yamagata Prefecture|ja|山形県}}. It enshrines over 48,000 spirits of those from Yamagata Prefecture who died in wars from the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} through the {{ill|Second Sino-Japanese War|ja|日中戦争}} and {{ill|World War II|ja|第二次世界大戦}}. == History == The shrine traces its origins to Meiji 2 (1869), when a hall was constructed in Yōka-chō, Yamagata City, to enshrine the spirits of ten {{ill|Satsuma Domain|ja|薩摩藩}} soldiers who died in the {{ill|Boshin War|ja|戊辰戦争}}. In Meiji 8, it was designated as Yamagata {{ill|Shōkonsha|ja|招魂社}}, and subsequently enshrined war dead from Yamagata Prefecture. In Meiji 22 (1889), it was relocated to Miyamachi, Yamagata City, but was destroyed by fire in a large blaze in 1911 (Meiji 44), and rebuilt in 1914 (Taishō 3). In Shōwa 9 (1934), it moved to its current location inside Chitose Park. In Shōwa 14 (1939), with institutional reforms, it was designated as an Interior Minister-approved Gokoku Jinja and named Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja. Under the Allied Occupation, from Shōwa 22 (1947) to Shōwa 27 (1952), it was called “Chitose-gū,” referencing Chitose Park. The current haiden was rebuilt in Heisei 6 (1994). == Hatsumōde (First Shrine Visit of the New Year) == Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja attracts the largest number of hatsumōde (New Year’s first visits) worshippers in Yamagata Prefecture, with about 130,000 visitors annually.[http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/history.shtml Official site: History (in Japanese)][http://yamagata-np.jp/news/200901/05/kj_2009010500051.php “91,6000 People Visit Shrines in the Prefecture for New Year: Up by 33,000 from Last Year”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 5, 2009), accessed September 7, 2011.[http://yamagata-np.jp/news/201101/04/kj_2011010400048.php “Over 1 Million Visit Shrines for Hatsumōde in Prefecture, Highest in a Decade”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 4, 2011), accessed September 7, 2011. The second most visited shrine is {{ill|Chōkai Gassan Ryōsho-gū|ja|鳥海月山両所宮}} in Yamagata City (~110,000 visitors). Only these two shrines surpass 100,000 visitors in the prefecture. == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/ Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja Official Site] {{Shinto Navbox}} {{Shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrines]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Yamagata (city)]] [[Category:History of Yamagata (city)]] == New years festival == The shrine has the largest [[Hatsumōde]] festival of [[Yamagata Prefecture]] with 130,000 people attending. Gokoku-jinja longshot.jpg|thumb|250px|Ōtorii (and haiden in the background)]] '''Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja''' (山形県護国神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Gokoku Shrine|ja|護国神社}}) located in {{ill|Yamagata (city)|ja|山形市}}, {{ill|Yamagata Prefecture|ja|山形県}}. It enshrines over 48,000 spirits of those from Yamagata Prefecture who died in wars from the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} through the {{ill|Second Sino-Japanese War|ja|日中戦争}} and {{ill|World War II|ja|第二次世界大戦}}. == History == The shrine traces its origins to Meiji 2 (1869), when a hall was constructed in Yōka-chō, Yamagata City, to enshrine the spirits of ten {{ill|Satsuma Domain|ja|薩摩藩}} soldiers who died in the {{ill|Boshin War|ja|戊辰戦争}}. In Meiji 8, it was designated as Yamagata {{ill|Shōkonsha|ja|招魂社}}, and subsequently enshrined war dead from Yamagata Prefecture. In Shōwa 14 (1939), with institutional reforms, it was designated as an Interior Minister-approved Gokoku Jinja and named Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja. Gokoku-jinja longshot.jpg|thumb|250px|Ōtorii (and haiden in the background)]] '''Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja''' (山形県護国神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Gokoku Shrine|ja|護国神社}}) located in {{ill|Yamagata (city)|ja|山形市}}, {{ill|Yamagata Prefecture|ja|山形県}}. It enshrines over 48,000 spirits of those from Yamagata Prefecture who died in wars from the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} through the {{ill|Second Sino-Japanese War|ja|日中戦争}} and {{ill|World War II|ja|第二次世界大戦}}. == History == The shrine traces its origins to Meiji 2 (1869), when a hall was constructed in Yōka-chō, Yamagata City, to enshrine the spirits of ten {{ill|Satsuma Domain|ja|薩摩藩}} soldiers who died in the {{ill|Boshin War|ja|戊辰戦争}}. In Meiji 8, it was designated as Yamagata {{ill|Shōkonsha|ja|招魂社}}, and subsequently enshrined war dead from Yamagata Prefecture. In Meiji 22 (1889), it was relocated to Miyamachi, Yamagata City, but was destroyed by fire in a large blaze in 1911 (Meiji 44), and rebuilt in 1914 (Taishō 3). In Shōwa 9 (1934), it moved to its current location inside Chitose Park. In Shōwa 14 (1939), with institutional reforms, it was designated as an Interior Minister-approved Gokoku Jinja and named Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja. Under the Allied Occupation, from Shōwa 22 (1947) to Shōwa 27 (1952), it was called “Chitose-gū,” referencing Chitose Park. The current haiden was rebuilt in Heisei 6 (1994). == Hatsumōde (First Shrine Visit of the New Year) == Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja attracts the largest number of hatsumōde (New Year’s first visits) worshippers in Yamagata Prefecture, with about 130,000 visitors annually.[http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/history.shtml Official site: History (in Japanese)][http://yamagata-np.jp/news/200901/05/kj_2009010500051.php “91,6000 People Visit Shrines in the Prefecture for New Year: Up by 33,000 from Last Year”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 5, 2009), accessed September 7, 2011.[http://yamagata-np.jp/news/201101/04/kj_2011010400048.php “Over 1 Million Visit Shrines for Hatsumōde in Prefecture, Highest in a Decade”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 4, 2011), accessed September 7, 2011. The second most visited shrine is {{ill|Chōkai Gassan Ryōsho-gū|ja|鳥海月山両所宮}} in Yamagata City (~110,000 visitors). Only these two shrines surpass 100,000 visitors in the prefecture. == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/ Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja Official Site] {{Shinto Navbox}} {{Shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Yamagata (city)]] [[Category:History of Yamagata (city)]] == New years festival == The shrine has the largest [[Hatsumōde]] festival of [[Yamagata Prefecture]] with 130,000 people attending. Gokoku-jinja longshot.jpg|thumb|250px|Ōtorii (and haiden in the background)]] '''Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja''' (山形県護国神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Gokoku Shrine|ja|護国神社}}) located in {{ill|Yamagata (city)|ja|山形市}}, {{ill|Yamagata Prefecture|ja|山形県}}. It enshrines over 48,000 spirits of those from Yamagata Prefecture who died in wars from the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} through the {{ill|Second Sino-Japanese War|ja|日中戦争}} and {{ill|World War II|ja|第二次世界大戦}}. == History == The shrine traces its origins to Meiji 2 (1869), when a hall was constructed in Yōka-chō, Yamagata City, to enshrine the spirits of ten {{ill|Satsuma Domain|ja|薩摩藩}} soldiers who died in the {{ill|Boshin War|ja|戊辰戦争}}. In Meiji 8, it was designated as Yamagata {{ill|Shōkonsha|ja|招魂社}}, and subsequently enshrined war dead from Yamagata Prefecture. In Meiji 22 (1889), it was relocated to Miyamachi, Yamagata City, but was destroyed by fire in a large blaze in 1911 (Meiji 44), and rebuilt in 1914 (Taishō 3). In Shōwa 9 (1934), it moved to its current location inside Chitose Park. In Shōwa 14 (1939), with institutional reforms, it was designated as an Interior Minister-approved Gokoku Jinja and named Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja. Under the Allied Occupation, from Shōwa 22 (1947) to Shōwa 27 (1952), it was called “Chitose-gū,” referencing Chitose Park. The current haiden was rebuilt in Heisei 6 (1994). == Hatsumōde (First Shrine Visit of the New Year) == Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja attracts the largest number of hatsumōde (New Year’s first visits) worshippers in Yamagata Prefecture, with about 130,000 visitors annually.[http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/history.shtml Official site: History (in Japanese)][http://yamagata-np.jp/news/200901/05/kj_2009010500051.php “91,6000 People Visit Shrines in the Prefecture for New Year: Up by 33,000 from Last Year”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 5, 2009), accessed September 7, 2011.[http://yamagata-np.jp/news/201101/04/kj_2011010400048.php “Over 1 Million Visit Shrines for Hatsumōde in Prefecture, Highest in a Decade”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 4, 2011), accessed September 7, 2011. The second most visited shrine is {{ill|Chōkai Gassan Ryōsho-gū|ja|鳥海月山両所宮}} in Yamagata City (~110,000 visitors). Only these two shrines surpass 100,000 visitors in the prefecture. == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/ Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja Official Site] {{Shinto Navbox}} {{Shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Yamagata (city)]] [[Category:History of Yamagata (city)]] == New years festival == The shrine has the largest [[Hatsumōde]] festival of [[Yamagata Prefecture]] with 130,000 people attending. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |doi=10.1093/jcs/32.3.527 |jstor=23917081 |issn=0021-969X}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja (Yamagata Prefectural Gokoku Shrine) | image = [[File:Yamagata Pref. Gokoku-jinja longshot.jpg|thumb|250px|Ōtorii (and haiden in the background)]] '''Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja''' (山形県護国神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Gokoku Shrine|ja|護国神社}}) located in {{ill|Yamagata (city)|ja|山形市}}, {{ill|Yamagata Prefecture|ja|山形県}}. It enshrines over 48,000 spirits of those from Yamagata Prefecture who died in wars from the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} through the {{ill|Second Sino-Japanese War|ja|日中戦争}} and {{ill|World War II|ja|第二次世界大戦}}. == History == The shrine traces its origins to Meiji 2 (1869), when a hall was constructed in Yōka-chō, Yamagata City, to enshrine the spirits of ten {{ill|Satsuma Domain|ja|薩摩藩}} soldiers who died in the {{ill|Boshin War|ja|戊辰戦争}}. In Meiji 8, it was designated as Yamagata {{ill|Shōkonsha|ja|招魂社}}, and subsequently enshrined war dead from Yamagata Prefecture. In Meiji 22 (1889), it was relocated to Miyamachi, Yamagata City, but was destroyed by fire in a large blaze in 1911 (Meiji 44), and rebuilt in 1914 (Taishō 3). In Shōwa 9 (1934), it moved to its current location inside Chitose Park. In Shōwa 14 (1939), with institutional reforms, it was designated as an Interior Minister-approved Gokoku Jinja and named Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja. Under the Allied Occupation, from Shōwa 22 (1947) to Shōwa 27 (1952), it was called “Chitose-gū,” referencing Chitose Park. The current haiden was rebuilt in Heisei 6 (1994). == Hatsumōde (First Shrine Visit of the New Year) == Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja attracts the largest number of hatsumōde (New Year’s first visits) worshippers in Yamagata Prefecture, with about 130,000 visitors annually.[http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/history.shtml Official site: History (in Japanese)][http://yamagata-np.jp/news/200901/05/kj_2009010500051.php “91,6000 People Visit Shrines in the Prefecture for New Year: Up by 33,000 from Last Year”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 5, 2009), accessed September 7, 2011.[http://yamagata-np.jp/news/201101/04/kj_2011010400048.php “Over 1 Million Visit Shrines for Hatsumōde in Prefecture, Highest in a Decade”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 4, 2011), accessed September 7, 2011. The second most visited shrine is {{ill|Chōkai Gassan Ryōsho-gū|ja|鳥海月山両所宮}} in Yamagata City (~110,000 visitors). Only these two shrines surpass 100,000 visitors in the prefecture. == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/ Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja Official Site] {{Shinto Navbox}} {{Shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Yamagata (city)]] [[Category:History of Yamagata (city)]] == New years festival == The shrine has the largest [[Hatsumōde]] festival of [[Yamagata Prefecture]] with 130,000 people attending. Gokoku-jinja longshot.jpg|thumb|250px|Ōtorii (and haiden in the background)]] '''Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja''' (山形県護国神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Gokoku Shrine|ja|護国神社}}) located in {{ill|Yamagata (city)|ja|山形市}}, {{ill|Yamagata Prefecture|ja|山形県}}. It enshrines over 48,000 spirits of those from Yamagata Prefecture who died in wars from the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} through the {{ill|Second Sino-Japanese War|ja|日中戦争}} and {{ill|World War II|ja|第二次世界大戦}}. == History == The shrine traces its origins to Meiji 2 (1869), when a hall was constructed in Yōka-chō, Yamagata City, to enshrine the spirits of ten {{ill|Satsuma Domain|ja|薩摩藩}} soldiers who died in the {{ill|Boshin War|ja|戊辰戦争}}. In Meiji 8, it was designated as Yamagata {{ill|Shōkonsha|ja|招魂社}}, and subsequently enshrined war dead from Yamagata Prefecture. In Meiji 22 (1889), it was relocated to Miyamachi, Yamagata City, but was destroyed by fire in a large blaze in 1911 (Meiji 44), and rebuilt in 1914 (Taishō 3). In Shōwa 9 (1934), it moved to its current location inside Chitose Park. In Shōwa 14 (1939), with institutional reforms, it was designated as an Interior Minister-approved Gokoku Jinja and named Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja. Under the Allied Occupation, from Shōwa 22 (1947) to Shōwa 27 (1952), it was called “Chitose-gū,” referencing Chitose Park. The current haiden was rebuilt in Heisei 6 (1994). == Hatsumōde (First Shrine Visit of the New Year) == Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja attracts the largest number of hatsumōde (New Year’s first visits) worshippers in Yamagata Prefecture, with about 130,000 visitors annually.[http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/history.shtml Official site: History (in Japanese)][http://yamagata-np.jp/news/200901/05/kj_2009010500051.php “91,6000 People Visit Shrines in the Prefecture for New Year: Up by 33,000 from Last Year”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 5, 2009), accessed September 7, 2011.[http://yamagata-np.jp/news/201101/04/kj_2011010400048.php “Over 1 Million Visit Shrines for Hatsumōde in Prefecture, Highest in a Decade”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 4, 2011), accessed September 7, 2011. The second most visited shrine is {{ill|Chōkai Gassan Ryōsho-gū|ja|鳥海月山両所宮}} in Yamagata City (~110,000 visitors). Only these two shrines surpass 100,000 visitors in the prefecture. == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/ Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja Official Site] {{Shinto Navbox}} {{Shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT::Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Yamagata (city)]] [[Category:History of Yamagata (city)]] == New years festival == The shrine has the largest [[Hatsumōde]] festival of [[Yamagata Prefecture]] with 130,000 people attending. [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it. It was founded in 1868, and is located in [[Yamagata Prefecture]].{{Cite web |last=Yassan |date=2021-11-29 |title=Tiger in Yamagata prefecture Gokoku shrine, Yamagata City 25km |url=https://gpsart.info/en/tohoku-2/tiger-in-yamagata-prefecture-gokoku-shrine-yamagata-city-25km/ |access-date=2023-11-27 |website=GPS Art .info |language=en-GB}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead. Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |doi=10.1093/jcs/32.3.527 |jstor=23917081 |issn=0021-969X}} It enshrines over 48,000 spirits of those from Yamagata Prefecture who died in wars from the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} through the {{ill|Second Sino-Japanese War|ja|日中戦争}} and {{ill|World War II|ja|第二次世界大戦}}. [[File:Yamagata Pref. Gokoku-jinja longshot.jpg|thumb|250px|Ōtorii (and haiden in the background)]] == History == The shrine traces its origins to Meiji 2 (1869), when a hall was constructed in Yōka-chō, Yamagata City, to enshrine the spirits of ten {{ill|Satsuma Domain|ja|薩摩藩}} soldiers who died in the {{ill|Boshin War|ja|戊辰戦争}}. In Meiji 8, it was designated as Yamagata {{ill|Shōkonsha|ja|招魂社}}, and subsequently enshrined war dead from Yamagata Prefecture. In Meiji 22 (1889), it was relocated to Miyamachi, Yamagata City, but was destroyed by fire in a large blaze in 1911 (Meiji 44), and rebuilt in 1914 (Taishō 3). In Shōwa 9 (1934), it moved to its current location inside Chitose Park. In Shōwa 14 (1939), with institutional reforms, it was designated as an Interior Minister-approved Gokoku Jinja and named Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja. Under the Allied Occupation, from Shōwa 22 (1947) to Shōwa 27 (1952), it was called “Chitose-gū,” referencing Chitose Park. The current haiden was rebuilt in Heisei 6 (1994). == Hatsumōde (First Shrine Visit of the New Year) == Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja attracts the largest number of hatsumōde (New Year’s first visits) worshippers in Yamagata Prefecture, with about 130,000 visitors annually.[http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/history.shtml Official site: History (in Japanese)][http://yamagata-np.jp/news/200901/05/kj_2009010500051.php “91,6000 People Visit Shrines in the Prefecture for New Year: Up by 33,000 from Last Year”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 5, 2009), accessed September 7, 2011.[http://yamagata-np.jp/news/201101/04/kj_2011010400048.php “Over 1 Million Visit Shrines for Hatsumōde in Prefecture, Highest in a Decade”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 4, 2011), accessed September 7, 2011. The second most visited shrine is {{ill|Chōkai Gassan Ryōsho-gū|ja|鳥海月山両所宮}} in Yamagata City (~110,000 visitors). Only these two shrines surpass 100,000 visitors in the prefecture. == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/ Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja Official Site] {{Shinto Navbox}} {{Shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT::Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Yamagata (city)]] [[Category:History of Yamagata (city)]] == New years festival == The shrine has the largest [[Hatsumōde]] festival of [[Yamagata Prefecture]] with 130,000 people attending. [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it. It was founded in 1868, and is located in [[Yamagata Prefecture]].{{Cite web |last=Yassan |date=2021-11-29 |title=Tiger in Yamagata prefecture Gokoku shrine, Yamagata City 25km |url=https://gpsart.info/en/tohoku-2/tiger-in-yamagata-prefecture-gokoku-shrine-yamagata-city-25km/ |access-date=2023-11-27 |website=GPS Art .info |language=en-GB}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead. Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |doi=10.1093/jcs/32.3.527 |jstor=23917081 |issn=0021-969X}} It enshrines over 48,000 spirits of those from Yamagata Prefecture who died in wars from the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} through the {{ill|Second Sino-Japanese War|ja|日中戦争}} and {{ill|World War II|ja|第二次世界大戦}}. [[File:Yamagata Pref. Gokoku-jinja longshot.jpg|thumb|250px|Ōtorii (and haiden in the background)]] == History == The shrine traces its origins to Meiji 2 (1869), when a hall was constructed in Yōka-chō, Yamagata City, to enshrine the spirits of ten {{ill|Satsuma Domain|ja|薩摩藩}} soldiers who died in the {{ill|Boshin War|ja|戊辰戦争}}. In Meiji 8, it was designated as Yamagata {{ill|Shōkonsha|ja|招魂社}}, and subsequently enshrined war dead from Yamagata Prefecture. In Meiji 22 (1889), it was relocated to Miyamachi, Yamagata City, but was destroyed by fire in a large blaze in 1911 (Meiji 44), and rebuilt in 1914 (Taishō 3). In Shōwa 9 (1934), it moved to its current location inside Chitose Park. In Shōwa 14 (1939), with institutional reforms, it was designated as an Interior Minister-approved Gokoku Jinja and named Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja. Under the Allied Occupation, from Shōwa 22 (1947) to Shōwa 27 (1952), it was called “Chitose-gū,” referencing Chitose Park. The current haiden was rebuilt in Heisei 6 (1994). == Hatsumōde (First Shrine Visit of the New Year) == {{DEFAULTSORT::Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Yamagata (city)]] [[Category:History of Yamagata (city)]] Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja attracts the largest number of hatsumōde (New Year’s first visits) worshippers in Yamagata Prefecture, with about 130,000 visitors annually.[http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/history.shtml Official site: History (in Japanese)][http://yamagata-np.jp/news/200901/05/kj_2009010500051.php “91,6000 People Visit Shrines in the Prefecture for New Year: Up by 33,000 from Last Year”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 5, 2009), accessed September 7, 2011.[http://yamagata-np.jp/news/201101/04/kj_2011010400048.php “Over 1 Million Visit Shrines for Hatsumōde in Prefecture, Highest in a Decade”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 4, 2011), accessed September 7, 2011. The second most visited shrine is {{ill|Chōkai Gassan Ryōsho-gū|ja|鳥海月山両所宮}} in Yamagata City (~110,000 visitors). Only these two shrines surpass 100,000 visitors in the prefecture. == New years festival == The shrine has the largest [[Hatsumōde]] festival of [[Yamagata Prefecture]] with 130,000 people attending. Second most is {{ill|Chōkai gassan ryōsho-gu|simple|Chōkai gassan ryōsho-gu|ja|鳥海月山両所宮|draft}} == See Also == * [[Controversies surrounding Yasukuni Shrine]] * [[Martyrs' shrines (China)|Martyr's [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it. It was founded in 1868, and is located in [[Yamagata Prefecture]].{{Cite web |last=Yassan |date=2021-11-29 |title=Tiger in Yamagata prefecture Gokoku shrine, Yamagata City 25km |url=https://gpsart.info/en/tohoku-2/tiger-in-yamagata-prefecture-gokoku-shrine-yamagata-city-25km/ |access-date=2023-11-27 |website=GPS Art .info |language=en-GB}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead. Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |doi=10.1093/jcs/32.3.527 |jstor=23917081 |issn=0021-969X}} It enshrines over 48,000 spirits of those from Yamagata Prefecture who died in wars from the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} through the {{ill|Second Sino-Japanese War|ja|日中戦争}} and {{ill|World War II|ja|第二次世界大戦}}. [[File:Yamagata Pref. Gokoku-jinja longshot.jpg|thumb|250px|Ōtorii (and haiden in the background)]] == History == The shrine traces its origins to Meiji 2 (1869), when a hall was constructed in Yōka-chō, Yamagata City, to enshrine the spirits of ten {{ill|Satsuma Domain|ja|薩摩藩}} soldiers who died in the {{ill|Boshin War|ja|戊辰戦争}}. In Meiji 8, it was designated as Yamagata {{ill|Shōkonsha|ja|招魂社}}, and subsequently enshrined war dead from Yamagata Prefecture. In Meiji 22 (1889), it was relocated to Miyamachi, Yamagata City, but was destroyed by fire in a large blaze in 1911 (Meiji 44), and rebuilt in 1914 (Taishō 3). In Shōwa 9 (1934), it moved to its current location inside Chitose Park. In Shōwa 14 (1939), with institutional reforms, it was designated as an Interior Minister-approved Gokoku Jinja and named Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja. Under the Allied Occupation, from Shōwa 22 (1947) to Shōwa 27 (1952), it was called “Chitose-gū,” referencing Chitose Park. The current haiden was rebuilt in Heisei 6 (1994). == Hatsumōde (First Shrine Visit of the New Year) == {{citation needed|Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Yamagata (city)]] [[Category:History of Yamagata (city)]] Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja attracts the largest number of hatsumōde (New Year’s first visits) worshippers in Yamagata Prefecture, with about 130,000 visitors annually.[http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/history.shtml Official site: History (in Japanese)][http://yamagata-np.jp/news/200901/05/kj_2009010500051.php “91,6000 People Visit Shrines in the Prefecture for New Year: Up by 33,000 from Last Year”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 5, 2009), accessed September 7, 2011.[http://yamagata-np.jp/news/201101/04/kj_2011010400048.php “Over 1 Million Visit Shrines for Hatsumōde in Prefecture, Highest in a Decade”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 4, 2011), accessed September 7, 2011. The second most visited shrine is {{ill|Chōkai Gassan Ryōsho-gū|ja|鳥海月山両所宮}} in Yamagata City (~110,000 visitors). Only these two shrines surpass 100,000 visitors in the prefecture. == New years festival == The shrine has the largest [[Hatsumōde]] festival of [[Yamagata Prefecture]] with 130,000 people attending. Second most is {{ill|Chōkai gassan ryōsho-gu|simple|Chōkai gassan ryōsho-gu|ja|鳥海月山両所宮|draft}} == See Also == * [[Controversies surrounding Yasukuni Shrine]] * [[Martyrs' shrines (China)|Martyr's Haiden | caption = | map_type = Japan Yamagata | coordinates = {{coord|38|15|45.23|N|140|20|49.86|E|scale:25000_region:JP-06_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja}} | location = Yakushimachi 2-8-75, {{ill|Yamagata (city)|ja|山形市|lt=Yamagata City}}, {{ill|Yamagata Prefecture|ja|山形県}}, Japan | deity = Over 48,045 war dead spirits (Gokoku no eirei) | type = Former Ministry of Interior-designated Gokoku Jinja, {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} | founded = {{ill|Meiji|ja|明治}} 2 ({{ill|1869|ja|1869年}}) | festival = {{ill|May 11|ja|5月11日}}, {{ill|November 2|ja|11月2日}} }} '''Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja''' (山形県護国神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Gokoku Shrine|ja|護国神社}}) located in {{ill|Yamagata (city)|ja|山形市}}, {{ill|Yamagata Prefecture|ja|山形県}}. [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it. It was founded in 1868, and is located in [[Yamagata Prefecture]].{{Cite web |last=Yassan |date=2021-11-29 |title=Tiger in Yamagata prefecture Gokoku shrine, Yamagata City 25km |url=https://gpsart.info/en/tohoku-2/tiger-in-yamagata-prefecture-gokoku-shrine-yamagata-city-25km/ |access-date=2023-11-27 |website=GPS Art .info |language=en-GB}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead. Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |doi=10.1093/jcs/32.3.527 |jstor=23917081 |issn=0021-969X}} It enshrines over 48,000 spirits of those from Yamagata Prefecture who died in wars from the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} through the {{ill|Second Sino-Japanese War|ja|日中戦争}} and {{ill|World War II|ja|第二次世界大戦}}. [[File:Yamagata Pref. Gokoku-jinja longshot.jpg|thumb|250px|Ōtorii (and haiden in the background)]] == History == The shrine traces its origins to Meiji 2 (1869), when a hall was constructed in Yōka-chō, Yamagata City, to enshrine the spirits of ten {{ill|Satsuma Domain|ja|薩摩藩}} soldiers who died in the {{ill|Boshin War|ja|戊辰戦争}}. In Meiji 8, it was designated as Yamagata {{ill|Shōkonsha|ja|招魂社}}, and subsequently enshrined war dead from Yamagata Prefecture. In Meiji 22 (1889), it was relocated to Miyamachi, Yamagata City, but was destroyed by fire in a large blaze in 1911 (Meiji 44), and rebuilt in 1914 (Taishō 3). In Shōwa 9 (1934), it moved to its current location inside Chitose Park. In Shōwa 14 (1939), with institutional reforms, it was designated as an Interior Minister-approved Gokoku Jinja and named Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja. Under the Allied Occupation, from Shōwa 22 (1947) to Shōwa 27 (1952), it was called “Chitose-gū,” referencing Chitose Park. The current haiden was rebuilt in Heisei 6 (1994). == Hatsumōde (First Shrine Visit of the New Year) == {{citation needed|Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Yamagata (city)]] [[Category:History of Yamagata (city)]] Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja attracts the largest number of hatsumōde (New Year’s first visits) worshippers in Yamagata Prefecture, with about 130,000 visitors annually.[http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/history.shtml Official site: History (in Japanese)][http://yamagata-np.jp/news/200901/05/kj_2009010500051.php “91,6000 People Visit Shrines in the Prefecture for New Year: Up by 33,000 from Last Year”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 5, 2009), accessed September 7, 2011.[http://yamagata-np.jp/news/201101/04/kj_2011010400048.php “Over 1 Million Visit Shrines for Hatsumōde in Prefecture, Highest in a Decade”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 4, 2011), accessed September 7, 2011. The second most visited shrine is {{ill|Chōkai Gassan Ryōsho-gū|ja|鳥海月山両所宮}} in Yamagata City (~110,000 visitors). Only these two shrines surpass 100,000 visitors in the prefecture. == New years festival == The shrine has the largest [[Hatsumōde]] festival of [[Yamagata Prefecture]] with 130,000 people attending. Second most is {{ill|Chōkai gassan ryōsho-gu|simple|Chōkai gassan ryōsho-gu|ja|鳥海月山両所宮|draft}} == See Also == * [[Controversies surrounding Yasukuni Shrine]] * [[Martyrs' shrines (China)|Martyr's In Meiji 8, it was designated as Yamagata {{ill|Shōkonsha|ja|招魂社}}, and subsequently enshrined war dead from Yamagata Prefecture. In Meiji 22 (1889), it was relocated to Miyamachi, Yamagata City, but was destroyed by fire in a large blaze in 1911 (Meiji 44), and rebuilt in 1914 (Taishō 3). In Shōwa 9 (1934), it moved to its current location inside Chitose Park. In Shōwa 14 (1939), with institutional reforms, it was designated as an Interior Minister-approved Gokoku Jinja and named Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja. Under the Allied Occupation, from Shōwa 22 (1947) to Shōwa 27 (1952), it was called “Chitose-gū,” referencing Chitose Park. The current haiden was rebuilt in Heisei 6 (1994). == Hatsumōde (First Shrine Visit of the New Year) == {{citation needed|Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Yamagata (city)]] [[Category:History of Yamagata (city)]] Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja attracts the largest number of hatsumōde (New Year’s first visits) worshippers in Yamagata Prefecture, with about 130,000 visitors annually.[http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/history.shtml Official site: History (in Japanese)][http://yamagata-np.jp/news/200901/05/kj_2009010500051.php “91,6000 People Visit Shrines in the Prefecture for New Year: Up by 33,000 from Last Year”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 5, 2009), accessed September 7, 2011.[http://yamagata-np.jp/news/201101/04/kj_2011010400048.php “Over 1 Million Visit Shrines for Hatsumōde in Prefecture, Highest in a Decade”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 4, 2011), accessed September 7, 2011. The second most visited shrine is {{ill|Chōkai Gassan Ryōsho-gū|ja|鳥海月山両所宮}} in Yamagata City (~110,000 visitors). Only these two shrines surpass 100,000 visitors in the prefecture. == New years festival == The shrine has the largest [[Hatsumōde]] festival of [[Yamagata Prefecture]] with 130,000 people attending. [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it. It was founded in 1868, and is located in [[Yamagata Prefecture]].{{Cite web |last=Yassan |date=2021-11-29 |title=Tiger in Yamagata prefecture Gokoku shrine, Yamagata City 25km |url=https://gpsart.info/en/tohoku-2/tiger-in-yamagata-prefecture-gokoku-shrine-yamagata-city-25km/ |access-date=2023-11-27 |website=GPS Art .info |language=en-GB}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead. Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |doi=10.1093/jcs/32.3.527 |jstor=23917081 |issn=0021-969X}} It enshrines over 48,000 spirits of those from Yamagata Prefecture who died in wars from the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} through the {{ill|Second Sino-Japanese War|ja|日中戦争}} and {{ill|World War II|ja|第二次世界大戦}}. [[File:Yamagata Pref. Gokoku-jinja longshot.jpg|thumb|250px|Ōtorii (and haiden in the background)]] == History == The shrine traces its origins to Meiji 2 (1869), when a hall was constructed in Yōka-chō, Yamagata City, to enshrine the spirits of ten {{ill|Satsuma Domain|ja|薩摩藩}} soldiers who died in the {{ill|Boshin War|ja|戊辰戦争}}. In Meiji 8, it was designated as Yamagata {{ill|Shōkonsha|ja|招魂社}}, and subsequently enshrined war dead from Yamagata Prefecture. In Meiji 22 (1889), it was relocated to Miyamachi, Yamagata City, but was destroyed by fire in a large blaze in 1911 (Meiji 44), and rebuilt in 1914 (Taishō 3). In Shōwa 9 (1934), it moved to its current location inside Chitose Park. In Shōwa 14 (1939), with institutional reforms, it was designated as an Interior Minister-approved Gokoku Jinja and named Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja. Under the Allied Occupation, from Shōwa 22 (1947) to Shōwa 27 (1952), it was called “Chitose-gū,” referencing Chitose Park. The current haiden was rebuilt in Heisei 6 (1994). == Hatsumōde (First Shrine Visit of the New Year) == {{citation needed|Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Yamagata (city)]] [[Category:History of Yamagata (city)]] Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja attracts the largest number of hatsumōde (New Year’s first visits) worshippers in Yamagata Prefecture, with about 130,000 visitors annually.[http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/history.shtml Official site: History (in Japanese)][http://yamagata-np.jp/news/200901/05/kj_2009010500051.php “91,6000 People Visit Shrines in the Prefecture for New Year: Up by 33,000 from Last Year”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 5, 2009), accessed September 7, 2011.[http://yamagata-np.jp/news/201101/04/kj_2011010400048.php “Over 1 Million Visit Shrines for Hatsumōde in Prefecture, Highest in a Decade”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 4, 2011), accessed September 7, 2011. The second most visited shrine is {{ill|Chōkai Gassan Ryōsho-gū|ja|鳥海月山両所宮}} in Yamagata City (~110,000 visitors). Only these two shrines surpass 100,000 visitors in the prefecture. == New years festival == The shrine has the largest [[Hatsumōde]] festival of [[Yamagata Prefecture]] with 130,000 people attending. [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it. It was founded in 1868, and is located in [[Yamagata Prefecture]].{{Cite web |last=Yassan |date=2021-11-29 |title=Tiger in Yamagata prefecture Gokoku shrine, Yamagata City 25km |url=https://gpsart.info/en/tohoku-2/tiger-in-yamagata-prefecture-gokoku-shrine-yamagata-city-25km/ |access-date=2023-11-27 |website=GPS Art .info |language=en-GB}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead. Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |doi=10.1093/jcs/32.3.527 |jstor=23917081 |issn=0021-969X}} It enshrines over 48,000 spirits of those from Yamagata Prefecture who died in wars from the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} through the {{ill|Second Sino-Japanese War|ja|日中戦争}} and {{ill|World War II|ja|第二次世界大戦}}. [[File:Yamagata Pref. Gokoku-jinja longshot.jpg|thumb|250px|Ōtorii (and haiden in the background)]] == History == The shrine traces its origins to Meiji 2 (1869), when a hall was constructed in Yōka-chō, Yamagata City, to enshrine the spirits of ten {{ill|Satsuma Domain|ja|薩摩藩}} soldiers who died in the {{ill|Boshin War|ja|戊辰戦争}}. In Meiji 8, it was designated as Yamagata {{ill|Shōkonsha|ja|招魂社}}, and subsequently enshrined war dead from Yamagata Prefecture. In Meiji 22 (1889), it was relocated to Miyamachi, Yamagata City, but was destroyed by fire in a large blaze in 1911 (Meiji 44), and rebuilt in 1914 (Taishō 3). In Shōwa 9 (1934), it moved to its current location inside Chitose Park. In Shōwa 14 (1939), with institutional reforms, it was designated as an Interior Minister-approved Gokoku Jinja and named Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja. Under the Allied Occupation, from Shōwa 22 (1947) to Shōwa 27 (1952), it was called “Chitose-gū,” referencing Chitose Park. The current haiden was rebuilt in Heisei 6 (1994). == Hatsumōde (First Shrine Visit of the New Year) == {{citation needed|Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Yamagata (city)]] [[Category:History of Yamagata (city)]] Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja attracts the largest number of hatsumōde (New Year’s first visits) worshippers in Yamagata Prefecture, with about 130,000 visitors annually.[http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/history.shtml Official site: History (in Japanese)][http://yamagata-np.jp/news/200901/05/kj_2009010500051.php “91,6000 People Visit Shrines in the Prefecture for New Year: Up by 33,000 from Last Year”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 5, 2009), accessed September 7, 2011.[http://yamagata-np.jp/news/201101/04/kj_2011010400048.php “Over 1 Million Visit Shrines for Hatsumōde in Prefecture, Highest in a Decade”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 4, 2011), accessed September 7, 2011. The second most visited shrine is {{ill|Chōkai Gassan Ryōsho-gū|ja|鳥海月山両所宮}} in Yamagata City (~110,000 visitors). Only these two shrines surpass 100,000 visitors in the prefecture. == New years festival == The shrine has the largest [[Hatsumōde]] festival of [[Yamagata Prefecture]] with 130,000 people attending. [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it. It was founded in 1868, and is located in [[Yamagata Prefecture]].{{Cite web |last=Yassan |date=2021-11-29 |title=Tiger in Yamagata prefecture Gokoku shrine, Yamagata City 25km |url=https://gpsart.info/en/tohoku-2/tiger-in-yamagata-prefecture-gokoku-shrine-yamagata-city-25km/ |access-date=2023-11-27 |website=GPS Art .info |language=en-GB}} It is a [[Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrine]], or a shrine dedicated to war dead. Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. They were renamed from [[Shōkonsha|Shokonsha]] in 1939.{{Cite journal |last=TAKAYAMA |first=K. PETER |date=1990 |title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081 |journal=Journal of Church and State |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=527–547 |doi=10.1093/jcs/32.3.527 |jstor=23917081 |issn=0021-969X}} It enshrines over 48,000 spirits of those from Yamagata Prefecture who died in wars from the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} through the {{ill|Second Sino-Japanese War|ja|日中戦争}} and {{ill|World War II|ja|第二次世界大戦}}. [[File:Yamagata Pref. Gokoku-jinja longshot.jpg|thumb|250px|Ōtorii (and haiden in the background)]] == History == The shrine traces its origins to Meiji 2 (1869), when a hall was constructed in Yōka-chō, Yamagata City, to enshrine the spirits of ten {{ill|Satsuma Domain|ja|薩摩藩}} soldiers who died in the {{ill|Boshin War|ja|戊辰戦争}}. In Meiji 8, it was designated as Yamagata {{ill|Shōkonsha|ja|招魂社}}, and subsequently enshrined war dead from Yamagata Prefecture. In Meiji 22 (1889), it was relocated to Miyamachi, Yamagata City, but was destroyed by fire in a large blaze in 1911 (Meiji 44), and rebuilt in 1914 (Taishō 3). In Shōwa 9 (1934), it moved to its current location inside Chitose Park. In Shōwa 14 (1939), with institutional reforms, it was designated as an Interior Minister-approved Gokoku Jinja and named Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja. Under the Allied Occupation, from Shōwa 22 (1947) to Shōwa 27 (1952), it was called “Chitose-gū,” referencing Chitose Park. The current haiden was rebuilt in Heisei 6 (1994). == Hatsumōde (First Shrine Visit of the New Year) == {{citation needed|Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Yamagata (city)]] [[Category:History of Yamagata (city)]] Yamagata-ken Gokoku Jinja attracts the largest number of hatsumōde (New Year’s first visits) worshippers in Yamagata Prefecture, with about 130,000 visitors annually.[http://www.yamagataken-gokokujinja.jp/history.shtml Official site: History (in Japanese)][http://yamagata-np.jp/news/200901/05/kj_2009010500051.php “91,6000 People Visit Shrines in the Prefecture for New Year: Up by 33,000 from Last Year”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 5, 2009), accessed September 7, 2011.[http://yamagata-np.jp/news/201101/04/kj_2011010400048.php “Over 1 Million Visit Shrines for Hatsumōde in Prefecture, Highest in a Decade”] Yamagata Shimbun (January 4, 2011), accessed September 7, 2011. The second most visited shrine is {{ill|Chōkai Gassan Ryōsho-gū|ja|鳥海月山両所宮}} in Yamagata City (~110,000 visitors). Only these two shrines surpass 100,000 visitors in the prefecture. == New years festival == The shrine has the largest [[Hatsumōde]] festival of [[Yamagata Prefecture]] with 130,000 people attending. Second most is {{ill|Chōkai gassan ryōsho-gu|simple|Chōkai gassan ryōsho-gu|ja|鳥海月山両所宮|draft}} == See Also == * [[Controversies surrounding Yasukuni Shrine]] * [[Martyrs' shrines (China)|Martyr's
